newsitem.title: USA: Jacksonville, Fla., orders airport audit.
newsitem.headline: Jacksonville, Fla., orders airport audit.

text.p: City auditors were asked to review Jacksonville International Airport finances to determine whether the northeast Florida facility should be placed under control of a separate aviation authority, Florida Times-Union reported Tuesday.

City Council President Eric Smith asked auditor Bob Johnson to determine whether the Jacksonville Port Authroity, which owns and operates the airport, is using any airport revenue to suport seaport operations.
Under terms of airport revenue bonds issued in 1988, the port authority is prohibited from shifting airport revenues to its marine division without approval fom the airport's major authorities.
Smith also asked auditors to deterime whether the aviation authority is paying more than it should in administative costs to the port authroity.
He told the newspaper he has no evidence of impropriety but is "on a fishing expedition to see that the air side is getting all the dollars it is entitled."
Smith has already asked the Florida Legislature to establish a separate airport authority to manage Jacksonville International and two general aviation airports.
Port Authority Chairman Barbara Suddath Strickland said the funds are divided appropriately and that the authority's books are audited by an independent firm, Coopers & Lybrand.
